steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease and flour a 9x13-inch pan. Sift flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and cinnamon together in a large bowl. Set aside.

Beat sugar and eggs together in a large bowl until thick and pale. Stir in oil. Gradually mix in the flour mixture until combined. Fold in carrots and walnuts. Spread batter evenly in the prepared pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the cake comes out clean, about 40 to 45 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Cinnamon-Walnut Carrot Cake
raw_recipe.description: Everyone tells me this is the best carrot cake ever! Top with your favorite cream cheese frosting.

review.reviewBody: This turned out really well. I followed the suggestions of another reviewer and used 1 cup of unsweetened apple sauce and 1/3 cup of oil instead of the full amount of oil, and the cake turned out moist and delicious. I halved the sugar -- I think two cups would have been too much! Indeed, the cake was still sweet, and I feel that I could have reduced the sugar even more, especially since we used cream cheese frosting. This makes quite a lot of cake; in the future I may make halve the recipe and bake it in a loaf pan for our small family. We served seven people and still ended up with leftovers for ten more!

My first foray into making my favorite cake flavor. It was awesome! I made 3 round pans instead of a sheet pan and added raisins instead of nuts (son does not like nuts). Also took the suggestion of 1/3 cup of oil and 1 cup of my mother's homemade applesauce (YUM). Put two of the rounds in the freezer for a rainy day. Now I can't wait until it rains again!

Super good. Stayed moist for days. I used 2 tablespoons cinnamon instead of 2 teaspoons also added a can of pineapple tidbits which I strained first. 

I doubled the recipie I had lots of shredded carrots from my garden in my freezer. It made 24 cupcakes and 4 loaf cakes. Topped it all with cream chz frosting. So delicious.

I had a request for a carrot cake for a birthday with no raisins and this one fit the bill perfectly. Very moist, not too sweet, frosted with cream cheese icing and topped with extra walnuts (per request from the birthday boy). I did add extra cinnamon since we like cinnamon, a little less sugar and used unsweetened applesauce (1 cup) with 1/3 cup oil as some suggested. I’m glad I made this in a bundt pan; I think it would have been harder to frost. This is my new go-to recipe for carrot cake.

I only used 3/4 cup vegetable oil and it came out great! Everyone loved it. It was very moist and flavorful. I omitted the nuts and raisins and I topped it with cream cheese frosting.

I cooked it in two 9"round pans and it took 45 min to cook.

I can't stop eating this cake! Scarfing down my 3rd piece now. I made a couple of changes to the recipe. For half of the flour I used ground up soft white wheat berries to make it a bit more healthier. Instead of the oil, I used 1 cup applesauce and 1/3 cup melted coconut oil. I added in some shredded zucchini because this time of year, I have zucchini coming out my ears. Also added some extra cinnamon and some pumpkin spice, and also some mini choc. chips. It turned out moist and fluffy and too good with the cream cheese frosting.

Excellent cake, and I have been using this recipe for 15 years. BUT today, I made changes. 1 C oil instead of 1+1/3, 5 C chopped carrots instead of 4 C. Next time, I think I'll decrease the sugar by 1/2 c. Also, its VERY moist, so I may increase the flour 1/2 C. And, since I could still see the cake, I think I'll add 1/2 c more chopped carrots.

I also used apple sauce and cut oil. I also added extra spice I made these for a wedding and pipped succulents on top. They were huge hit! I added 3 tsp cinnamon, 1/2 tsp gloves, 1 tsp pumpkin spice and 1/8 tsp of all spice. I could had added more I love a rich spice flavor but it’s carrot cake. Cream cheese icing was amazing!

I made this today for my mother's birthday. I followed some other reviewer's suggestion by using 1 cup applesauce and 1/3 cup oil, 1 cup sugar, and added a pinch of nutmeg. The flavor was fabulous but the cake was a little on the heavy side. I will definitely make it again but will play with the oil to applesauce ratio. 

 I made this again using less than 1 cup oil (I had no applesauce) and it turned out great again. I used brown sugar and white. My almost 2 year old is tearing it up as I type.:-)

Pretty good! But too crumbly and not as moist as I like. Will follow recipe specs re 11/3 cups of veggie oil next time; instead of cutting back on oil as so many reviewers suggested. Cut back cinnamon to 1 1/2 tsp & added a generous pinch of ground cloves & ground ginger, 1/3 cup crushed fresh pineapple, 3/4 cup raisins, for richer carroty taste. We can’t have & don’t like nuts in cakes, so no nuts. Can substitute unsweetened coconut flakes for texture and flavour. Great taste and not too sweet. Will make again with these adjustments.

I'm not a huge fan of carrot cake until NOW! Made some modifications based on someone's request (this was a Birthday cake request) decreased the sugar, only used 1/3 of what it called for, upped the carrots by 1 cup and it was RIDICULOUS! So moist and delicious!!!! Topped it off with cream cheese frosting, but I tell ya, it didn't need anything! I could have eaten 1/2 of it myself! GREAT recipe!!!
Delicious! I used 1/3 cup of apple sauce and 1cup of oil. Made Aunt Becky’s cream cheese frosting for the win!
i love , plus add to mashed bananas and some almonds and it came out soft and moist delicious, a friend asked me for the recipe , instead i use light brown sugar

I was VERY happy with the results. Cake was wonderful and moist. I used the correctly sized 9x13 pan and was a bit concerned when it took over 60 minutes to cook thoroughly but well worth it. Will definitely make it again.
Best carrot cake ever. Super moist and the perfect sweetness. Everyone raves about it everytime I make it.

Excellent cake! Dense and moist and delicious. The center of mine took a long time to bake. I will use this recipe again and use a bundt pan (instead of the recommended 9x13) which will help it bake more evenly, I think. I will add that this recipe is very forgiving. Despite the fact that I made a few mistakes in the process, the cake turned out great.
My wife said this was THE BEST cake I've ever made. Perfectly moist, with just the right amount of spice(s - I always add ginger & nutmeg to cinnamon when baking).
I made this in two 8" pans. Both pans sunk in the middle. It came out very oily when I took them out of the pan to put them on the cooling rack. Will definitely not make again.
It came out great easy recipe 😋 👌 and delicious
